name: MASTER AUTONOMOUS DEVELOPMENT PROMPT PROJECT: WESTVOICE

messages.content:
MASTER AUTONOMOUS DEVELOPMENT PROMPT

PROJECT: WESTVOICE AI

An AI-powered West African Multilingual Voice Recognition, Translation and Community Language Preservation Platform

1. YOUR ROLE

You are the principal autonomous software architect, senior full-stack engineer, AI engineer, UI/UX designer, QA engineer, DevOps engineer and technical project manager responsible for building WestVoice AI.

Your assignment is to independently plan, architect, develop, test, debug, deploy and document a complete production-ready web application.

You are expected to operate with maximum reasonable autonomy and minimal supervision.

Do not merely generate a project plan, prototype or static interface.

Build a genuinely functional application with working frontend, backend, database, Gemini integrations, community contribution functionality and deployment configuration.

Use your available capabilities, including:

* Terminal and command-line tools.
* Browser automation.
* Code editor.
* Multiple specialized agents where beneficial.
* Automated testing.
* Git and GitHub.
* Cloud deployment tools.

Make reasonable engineering decisions independently.

Only request my intervention when an external authorization, payment, API credential, account permission or irreversible action is required.

Do not stop unnecessarily to ask questions about ordinary implementation decisions.

⸻

2. PRODUCT VISION

WestVoice AI is a multilingual AI-powered platform designed to improve communication, accessibility and language preservation across West Africa.

The platform will enable users to:

1. Record speech in supported West African languages.
2. Upload existing audio recordings.
3. Convert spoken language into written text.
4. Translate transcriptions between supported languages.
5. Identify spoken languages where supported.
6. Preserve original transcriptions.
7. Contribute new words, phrases, dialects and pronunciations.
8. Help improve language recognition and translation through community participation.

The long-term vision is to build a valuable language resource for underserved African languages and eventually support additional African regions.

This should be developed as a scalable technology product rather than a simple demonstration of an AI API.

⸻

3. INITIAL LANGUAGE SUPPORT

Build the platform with the following initial language catalogue:

1. Hausa
2. Yoruba
3. Igbo
4. Fulfulde/Fula
5. Wolof
6. Bambara
7. Akan/Twi
8. Ewe
9. English
10. French

Design the architecture so that additional languages, dialects and regional variations can be introduced without restructuring the application.

IMPORTANT:

Do not assume that every language has identical recognition capabilities.

Maintain a configurable language registry containing:

* Language name.
* ISO language code where applicable.
* Alternative names.
* Supported dialects.
* Transcription support status.
* Translation support status.
* Automatic detection support.
* Available pronunciation resources.
* Verification status.

Allow the administrator to enable, disable or modify language support.

Do not advertise unverified language accuracy.

⸻

4. TECHNOLOGY STACK

Use a maintainable modern architecture.

Frontend

* React.
* TypeScript.
* Vite or another suitable modern frontend framework.
* Tailwind CSS.
* Accessible reusable components.
* Responsive mobile-first design.

Backend

* Python Django REST Framework OR Node.js/TypeScript.

Choose the architecture that offers the best integration with the Gemini API and supports the community language database.

Prefer a clean separation between application logic, AI services and database operations.

Database

* PostgreSQL.
* Proper relational models.
* Database migrations.
* Indexing.
* Secure user relationships.

AI

* Google’s official Gemini API.
* Official Google GenAI SDK.
* Gemini speech transcription model, using Gemini 3.5 Transcribe where available.
* Suitable Gemini Flash model for translation.
* Configurable model selection through environment variables.

Never hardcode model names throughout the application.

Deployment

* Google Cloud Run.
* PostgreSQL managed database.
* GitHub version control.
* Secure environment configuration.

Keep the application container-ready.

⸻

5. CORE MODULE: VOICE TRANSCRIPTION

Build a complete voice-to-text experience.

Audio input

Users must be able to:

* Record directly through their browser microphone.
* Pause and resume recording where supported.
* Stop recording.
* Preview recorded audio.
* Delete and re-record.
* Upload existing audio files.

Support common audio formats, including WAV, MP3, M4A and WebM where compatible with the processing pipeline.

Implement audio validation, size limits and duration limits.

Language selection

Provide:

* Source language selection.
* Automatic language detection where supported.
* Target language selection.
* Dialect selection where available.

Transcription

Use Gemini speech recognition to convert speech into written text.

Display:

* Original transcription.
* Detected language.
* Processing status.
* Relevant timestamps where available.
* Speaker separation where supported.

Allow users to edit the transcription.

Preserve the original machine-generated transcription separately from user corrections.

Translation

Translate the transcription into the selected target language.

The translation service must:

* Preserve meaning and context.
* Avoid unnecessary literal translation.
* Respect regional expressions.
* Handle idioms where possible.
* Preserve names and technical terms.
* Avoid inventing translations for unknown words.

Display original and translated text side by side.

Provide:

* Copy.
* Download.
* Edit.
* Translate again.
* Report incorrect transcription or translation.

Keep transcription and translation as separate backend services.

⸻

6. CORE MODULE: COMMUNITY LANGUAGE LAB

THIS IS A MAJOR FEATURE OF WESTVOICE AI.

Create a dedicated navigation tab called:

COMMUNITY LANGUAGE LAB

Its purpose is to allow native speakers and knowledgeable community members to contribute to the preservation and improvement of West African languages.

Do not treat this as an ordinary comment section.

It must function as a structured multilingual community language knowledge base.

A. Word Contribution

Users should be able to submit:

* New words.
* Regional expressions.
* Slang.
* Idioms.
* Proverbs.
* Traditional expressions.
* Alternative spellings.
* New meanings for existing words.
* Dialect-specific vocabulary.

Every submission should capture:

1. Word or expression.
2. Language.
3. Dialect or regional variation.
4. Meaning in English.
5. Meaning in French where available.
6. Example sentence.
7. Context of usage.
8. Alternative spellings.
9. Contributor notes.

B. Pronunciation Contribution

Allow local speakers to record the pronunciation of contributed words.

Each contribution should support:

* Audio recording.
* Audio playback.
* Written pronunciation guidance.
* Regional accent or dialect.
* Speaker-provided context.

Do not automatically assume that one pronunciation represents an entire language.

Allow multiple pronunciation recordings for the same word.

C. Phrase and Sentence Contributions

Allow users to submit complete phrases and sentences with translations.

Example:

Hausa phrase:
[Example Hausa expression]

English meaning:
[Meaning]

Context:
[When and how it is used]

This will help establish context-sensitive translation resources.

D. Community Validation

Implement a contribution review system.

Users should be able to:

* Suggest corrections.
* Confirm an existing word.
* Dispute an incorrect definition.
* Suggest another dialect.
* Validate pronunciations.
* Vote on the usefulness or correctness of contributions.

Contributions must have statuses:

* Pending.
* Under review.
* Approved.
* Rejected.
* Needs correction.

Implement moderator approval before contributions enter the verified language knowledge base.

Prevent duplicate submissions where practical.

E. Contributor Profiles

Create contributor profiles containing:

* Username.
* Languages contributed.
* Dialects contributed.
* Number of submitted words.
* Approved contributions.
* Validation activities.
* Contribution points.
* Achievement badges.

Introduce a contribution leaderboard to encourage participation.

Avoid rewarding quantity at the expense of accuracy.

F. Searchable Language Dictionary

Build a searchable dictionary from approved contributions.

Users should be able to:

* Search words.
* Search meanings.
* Filter by language.
* Filter by dialect.
* View example sentences.
* Listen to pronunciation recordings.
* Compare regional variations.
* Suggest corrections.

Create a public language knowledge base that grows as the community contributes.

⸻

7. CONNECT COMMUNITY KNOWLEDGE TO GEMINI

This is one of the most important architectural requirements.

Community contributions must have a practical impact on transcription and translation quality.

Create a separate Language Knowledge Service.

Its responsibilities include:

1. Retrieve verified vocabulary relevant to the selected language.
2. Retrieve dialect-specific expressions.
3. Retrieve pronunciation references where relevant.
4. Retrieve approved example sentences.
5. Supply relevant contextual information to Gemini during transcription or translation.
6. Allow administrators to update the knowledge base without changing application code.

Transcription integration

When processing audio:

* Identify the selected language.
* Retrieve relevant verified vocabulary.
* Supply appropriate vocabulary hints to the transcription model where supported.
* Preserve the original audio and machine transcription.
* Allow users to submit corrections.

Translation integration

Before translation:

* Retrieve relevant approved expressions.
* Include regional meanings and context.
* Provide the information as contextual guidance to Gemini.
* Preserve the intended meaning of dialect-specific words.

Important distinction

Community contributions must NOT automatically modify Gemini’s underlying model weights.

Implement a modular improvement architecture that initially uses:

* Verified vocabulary retrieval.
* Contextual prompting.
* Translation memory.
* Approved example sentences.
* Pronunciation references.

Design the system so that future versions can support:

* Dataset generation.
* Human-reviewed training corpora.
* Fine-tuning compatible open-source models.
* Language-specific evaluation datasets.
* Dedicated African language speech models.

Keep the community knowledge base independent of the Gemini provider.

This will allow us to integrate other AI providers or self-hosted language models in the future.

⸻

8. USER ACCOUNTS AND ROLES

Implement secure authentication.

User roles:

Guest

* Access basic transcription functionality.
* Access public translations and dictionary entries.
* Browse approved language resources.

Registered Contributor

* Submit words and phrases.
* Upload pronunciation recordings.
* Participate in validation.
* Maintain a contributor profile.
* Track contributions.

Moderator

* Review submissions.
* Approve or reject contributions.
* Resolve disputes.
* Flag inappropriate content.
* Manage duplicate entries.

Administrator

* Full application management.
* Manage users and roles.
* Manage languages and dialects.
* Manage contributions.
* Configure Gemini models.
* Monitor API usage.
* Manage platform settings.
* View analytics.

Implement appropriate authorization at both frontend and backend levels.

⸻

9. MAIN APPLICATION INTERFACE

Build a modern, polished and professional SaaS interface.

Use a distinctive visual identity for WestVoice AI.

Suggested aesthetic:

* Deep navy and blue.
* Subtle African-inspired design elements.
* Modern typography.
* Clean layouts.
* Accessible contrast.
* Smooth but restrained animations.
* Professional icons.
* Responsive navigation.

Avoid stereotypical or excessive cultural decoration.

Main navigation

Include:

1. Home.
2. Voice Translator.
3. Community Language Lab.
4. Language Dictionary.
5. My Contributions.
6. History.
7. Profile.
8. Admin Dashboard (authorized administrators only).

Homepage

The homepage should communicate the platform’s purpose immediately.

Include:

* Product introduction.
* Start translating button.
* Supported languages.
* How it works.
* Community contribution introduction.
* Recently approved words.
* Community statistics.

Voice Translator page

Include:

* Source language selector.
* Target language selector.
* Microphone recording.
* Audio upload.
* Transcription panel.
* Translation panel.
* Processing indicators.
* Copy and download controls.

Community Language Lab page

Include:

* Submit a new word.
* Submit a phrase.
* Record pronunciation.
* Explore community submissions.
* Review pending contributions where authorized.
* Contributor leaderboard.
* Search and filter functionality.

Dictionary page

Include:

* Word search.
* Language filters.
* Dialect filters.
* Meaning.
* Example sentences.
* Pronunciation playback.
* Regional variations.

⸻

10. ADDITIONAL FEATURES

Implement the following where practical without compromising the core MVP.

Translation history

Allow registered users to view previous translations.

Text-to-speech

Allow users to listen to translated text using a suitable available speech synthesis provider.

Do not claim support for voices that have not been verified.

Audio privacy

* Do not permanently store recordings by default.
* Use temporary storage for processing.
* Delete temporary files after processing.
* Obtain explicit consent before storing pronunciation contributions.
* Make deletion policies clear.

Feedback

Allow users to report:

* Incorrect transcription.
* Incorrect translation.
* Unsupported words.
* Incorrect language detection.

Use feedback to identify language quality problems.

⸻

11. DATABASE ARCHITECTURE

Create a properly normalized PostgreSQL database.

At minimum, design models for:

* Users.
* User profiles.
* Roles and permissions.
* Languages.
* Dialects.
* Transcription sessions.
* Translation sessions.
* Translation history.
* Community word entries.
* Phrase entries.
* Pronunciation recordings.
* Contribution reviews.
* Community votes.
* Corrections.
* Contributor achievements.
* Translation feedback.
* System configuration.

Use appropriate relationships, indexes, constraints and audit timestamps.

Maintain version history for approved language entries so that corrections do not silently destroy previous information.

⸻

12. SECURITY AND RELIABILITY

Implement:

* Secure API key management.
* Server-side Gemini API calls.
* Environment-based configuration.
* Authentication and authorization.
* Input validation.
* File validation.
* Rate limiting.
* Request size limits.
* Secure audio handling.
* Database constraints.
* Error logging.
* Basic monitoring.
* Protection against common web vulnerabilities.

Never expose GEMINI_API_KEY in frontend code.

Never allow unmoderated community contributions to silently become verified language resources.

Prevent malicious audio uploads and unauthorized file access.

Use reasonable usage limits to prevent unexpected API expenditure.

⸻

13. TESTING REQUIREMENTS

Testing is mandatory.

Do not declare the application complete simply because it compiles.

Test the following:

Frontend

* Desktop layout.
* Mobile layout.
* Recording controls.
* Audio uploads.
* Language selectors.
* Transcription display.
* Translation display.
* Dictionary search.
* Contribution submission.

Backend

* Authentication.
* Authorization.
* Database operations.
* Gemini integration.
* File validation.
* Error handling.
* Community moderation.
* Dictionary retrieval.
* Language knowledge retrieval.

AI functionality

Use actual Gemini API requests when credentials are available.

Test each language independently.

Do not fabricate successful language tests.

Record the limitations of languages that perform poorly.

Establish a process for native-speaker evaluation.

Separate transcription accuracy from translation accuracy.

⸻

14. DEPLOYMENT

Prepare and deploy the application using Google Cloud Run.

Use PostgreSQL through an appropriate managed database service.

Configure production environment variables securely.

Prepare Docker configuration if necessary.

Connect GitHub when authorized.

Ensure that:

* The production frontend loads.
* Backend APIs respond.
* Database connectivity works.
* Gemini integration works.
* Audio uploads work.
* Community contributions work.
* Dictionary search works.
* Authentication works.

Test the deployed application using its actual public URL.

Do not report deployment as successful without verifying it.

If deployment requires payment authorization or account permissions, complete everything possible before requesting my intervention.

⸻

15. DEVELOPMENT STRATEGY

Work in stages, but operate autonomously.

Stage 1: Foundation

* Project architecture.
* Database.
* Authentication.
* Main interface.
* Language registry.

Stage 2: AI Translator

* Audio recording.
* Audio upload.
* Gemini transcription.
* Gemini translation.
* Result management.

Stage 3: Community Language Lab

* Word submissions.
* Phrase submissions.
* Pronunciation recording.
* Contributor profiles.
* Moderation.
* Dictionary.

Stage 4: AI Knowledge Integration

* Verified vocabulary retrieval.
* Dialect-specific context.
* Translation memory.
* Contextual Gemini prompts.

Stage 5: Quality Assurance

* Automated testing.
* Browser testing.
* Security checks.
* AI quality evaluation.
* Bug fixing.

Stage 6: Deployment

* Production configuration.
* GitHub.
* Cloud Run.
* Database connectivity.
* Production verification.

Do not sacrifice the functionality of the core translator to implement unnecessary extras.

If time or resources are constrained, prioritize a working translator and functional Community Language Lab, then complete secondary features.

⸻

16. FINAL DELIVERABLES

I expect you to deliver:

1. A complete working WestVoice AI web application.
2. Responsive frontend.
3. Functional backend.
4. Gemini speech transcription integration.
5. Gemini translation integration.
6. Configurable West African language registry.
7. Community Language Lab.
8. Community word and phrase contribution system.
9. Pronunciation recording functionality.
10. Contribution moderation.
11. Searchable language dictionary.
12. Verified community knowledge integration with Gemini.
13. Authentication and role management.
14. PostgreSQL database.
15. Automated tests.
16. GitHub repository when authorized.
17. Production deployment on Cloud Run when authorized.
18. Complete README and technical documentation.

At completion, provide:

* Project architecture.
* Implemented functionality.
* Test results.
* Supported and verified languages.
* Known limitations.
* Outstanding actions requiring my authorization.
* GitHub repository.
* Live application URL, if deployment succeeded.

⸻

17. AUTONOMY INSTRUCTIONS

You have authority to make routine engineering decisions independently.

Do not repeatedly ask me to approve ordinary code changes.

Do not stop after creating the frontend.

Do not replace working functionality with mock data.

Do not claim that Gemini integrations work unless they have been tested with actual API credentials.

Do not invent language support or accuracy statistics.

Do not expose secrets.

Do not incur paid expenditure or make irreversible cloud account changes without authorization.

When an external dependency blocks progress, complete all independent tasks and identify the precise intervention needed.

Use specialized agents where doing so improves execution speed and quality.

Maintain a clear implementation checklist.

Test after every major integration.

Fix problems before moving forward.

Your objective is to deliver a working, maintainable, extensible and publicly accessible West African language technology platform.

BEGIN BY INSPECTING THE ENVIRONMENT, ESTABLISHING THE PROJECT ARCHITECTURE AND EXECUTING THE DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

DO NOT STOP AT PLANNING.
BUILD THE PRODUCT.
Please commit all staged changes with a descriptive commit message
All changes have been committed and saved. Everything is up to date.
